cemc-galois-2010-01b.title: Saving per minute
cemc-galois-2010-01b.body:
The new showerhead uses $18 - 13 = 5$ L less per minute, so in 10 minutes it uses $50$ L less.

**Answer: 50 L**

cemc-galois-2010-01b.title: Compare totals
cemc-galois-2010-01b.body:
Old: $18 \times 10 = 180$ L. New: $13 \times 10 = 130$ L. Difference: $50$ L.

**Answer: 50 L**

cemc-galois-2010-01c.title: Water saved, then cost
cemc-galois-2010-01c.body:
In 15 minutes she saves $15 \times 5 = 75$ L. At 8 cents per 100 L, that is $\frac{75}{100} \times 8 = 6$ cents.

**Answer: 6 cents**

cemc-galois-2010-01d.title: Saving per minute
cemc-galois-2010-01d.body:
She saves 5 L per minute, worth $\frac{5}{100} \times 8 = 0.4$ cents per minute. To save \$30 = 3000 cents takes $3000 \div 0.4 = 7500$ minutes.

**Answer: 7500 minutes**

cemc-galois-2010-01d.title: Scale up part (c)
cemc-galois-2010-01d.body:
15 minutes save 6 cents. Since $3000 \div 6 = 500$, she needs $500 \times 15 = 7500$ minutes.

**Answer: 7500 minutes**

cemc-galois-2010-02a.title: Trapezoid
cemc-galois-2010-02a.body:
$QA$ and $OB$ are both horizontal, so $QABO$ is a trapezoid with parallel sides $QA = 2$ and $OB = 12$ and height $QO = 12$. Area $= \frac12 (2 + 12)(12) = 84$.

**Answer: 84**

cemc-galois-2010-02a.title: Rectangle plus triangle
cemc-galois-2010-02a.body:
Let $T = (2, 0)$. Rectangle $QATO$ has area $2 \times 12 = 24$, and right triangle $ATB$ has area $\frac12 (10)(12) = 60$. Total $84$.

**Answer: 84**

cemc-galois-2010-02b.title: Right triangle
cemc-galois-2010-02b.body: $\triangle COB$ is right-angled at $O$ with legs $OB = 12$ and $OC = p$: area $= \frac12 (12)(p) = 6p$.

cemc-galois-2010-02c.title: Right triangle
cemc-galois-2010-02c.body: $\triangle QCA$ is right-angled at $Q$ with legs $QA = 2$ and $QC = 12 - p$: area $= \frac12 (2)(12 - p) = 12 - p$.

cemc-galois-2010-02d.title: Subtract the corner triangles
cemc-galois-2010-02d.body:
$\triangle ABC$ is $QABO$ minus $\triangle COB$ and $\triangle QCA$:

$$84 - 6p - (12 - p) = 72 - 5p = 27 \implies p = 9.$$

**Answer: $p = 9$**

cemc-galois-2010-03a.title: Elimination
cemc-galois-2010-03a.body:
Adding the equations: $2x = 52$, so $x = 26$. Then $y = 42 - 26 = 16$.

**Answer: $(x, y) = (26, 16)$**

cemc-galois-2010-03a.title: Substitution
cemc-galois-2010-03a.body:
From the second equation $x = y + 10$. Then $2y + 10 = 42$, $y = 16$, $x = 26$.

**Answer: $(26, 16)$**

cemc-galois-2010-03b.title: Add the equations
cemc-galois-2010-03b.body: Adding gives $2x = p + q$. Since $p$ is even and $q$ is odd, $p + q$ is odd. But $2x$ is even for every integer $x$. So there is no integer $x$, let alone a positive integer solution. ∎

cemc-galois-2010-03b.title: Same parity
cemc-galois-2010-03b.body: For integers $x, y$, the numbers $x + y$ and $x - y$ differ by $2y$, an even number, so they always have the same parity. But $p$ and $q$ have different parities. ∎

cemc-galois-2010-03c.title: Factor pairs of the same parity
cemc-galois-2010-03c.body:
$(x + y)(x - y) = 420$ with $x + y > x - y > 0$ (both positive since $x + y > 0$ and the product is positive). By part (b), $x + y$ and $x - y$ must have the same parity; since $420$ is even, both must be even.

Since $420 = 4 \cdot 105$, write $x + y = 2m$, $x - y = 2n$ with $mn = 105$, $m > n$: $(m, n) = (105, 1), (35, 3), (21, 5), (15, 7)$. Then $x = m + n$, $y = m - n$:

| $x + y$ | $x - y$ | $x$ | $y$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 210 | 2 | 106 | 104 |
| 70 | 6 | 38 | 32 |
| 42 | 10 | 26 | 16 |
| 30 | 14 | 22 | 8 |

**Answer: $(106, 104), (38, 32), (26, 16), (22, 8)$**

cemc-galois-2010-04a.title: Same height
cemc-galois-2010-04a.body:
Let $h$ be the distance from $P$ to line $QR$. It is the height of both triangles. So

$$\frac{|\triangle PQT|}{|\triangle PTR|} = \frac{\frac12 \cdot 6 \cdot h}{\frac12 \cdot 10 \cdot h} = \frac{6}{10} = \frac35. \;∎$$

cemc-galois-2010-04b.title: Work outwards with base ratios
cemc-galois-2010-04b.body:
Use the fact from (a): triangles with the same apex and bases on one line have areas in the ratio of their bases. Write $|XYZ|$ for the area of $\triangle XYZ$.

- On $AD$ with apex $E$: $|AEF| : |DEF| = AF : FD = 3 : 1$, so $|AEF| = 51$ and $|AED| = 68$.
- On $AC$ with apex $D$: $|ECD| : |AED| = EC : AE = 2 : 1$, so $|ECD| = 136$ and $|ADC| = 204$.
- On $BC$ with apex $A$: $|ABD| = |ADC|$ since $BD = DC$, so $|ABC| = 408$.

**Answer: 408**

cemc-galois-2010-04c.title: Area ratios along each cevian
cemc-galois-2010-04c.body:
Let $a = |PYV|$, $b = |PZU|$, $c = |UXP|$, $d = |XVP|$.

- $\frac{|PYV|}{|PYW|} = \frac{VY}{YW} = \frac43$, so $a = 40$.
- Along $UW$, triangles with apex $V$ and with apex $P$ have the same base ratio $WZ : ZU$:
  $\frac{|VZW|}{|VZU|} = \frac{|PZW|}{|PZU|}$, i.e. $\frac{35 + 30 + 40}{b + c + d} = \frac{35}{b}$, so $b + c + d = 3b$ and $c + d = 2b$.
- Along $VW$ with apex $U$: $\frac{|UVY|}{|UYW|} = \frac43$, i.e. $3(40 + c + d) = 4(30 + 35 + b)$. With $c + d = 2b$: $120 + 6b = 260 + 4b$, so $b = 70$ and $c + d = 140$.
- Along $UV$ with apexes $W$ and $P$: $\frac{|UXW|}{|XVW|} = \frac{|UXP|}{|XVP|}$, i.e. $\frac{35 + 70 + c}{30 + 40 + d} = \frac{c}{d}$, giving $105d = 70c$, $d = \frac23 c$.

Then $c + \frac23 c = 140$, so $c = 84$.

**Answer: 84**

cemc-galois-2010-04c.title: Finish with Ceva's theorem
cemc-galois-2010-04c.body:
As in Solution 1, $a = 40$, $b = 70$, so $\frac{WZ}{ZU} = \frac{|PZW|}{|PZU|} = \frac{35}{70} = \frac12$ and $c + d = 140$.

By Ceva's theorem for the concurrent cevians $UY$, $VZ$, $WX$:

$$\frac{UX}{XV} \cdot \frac{VY}{YW} \cdot \frac{WZ}{ZU} = 1 \implies \frac{UX}{XV} = \frac{3}{4} \cdot 2 = \frac32.$$

Triangles $UXP$ and $XVP$ share the apex $P$, so $c : d = 3 : 2$, and $c = \frac35 \cdot 140 = 84$.

**Answer: 84**
